BACKUP-1.title: Memory.Promote drops the parent history, so a third timeline's history file omits every earlier ancestor

BACKUP-2.title: Memory.Oldest_Restart_LSN treats restart LSN zero as no candidate and discards WAL a live slot needs

BACKUP-3.title: Memory.Append rebases a fully retained-away store, moving Current_LSN backwards and reusing WAL positions

BACKUP-4.title: Persistence.Generation keeps returning the stale nonzero lease after a slot is released

BACKUP-5.title: Prepared_Consumer.Prepare overwrites the Target_Applied marker for the same GID, defeating the replay guard

BACKUP-6.title: Memory.Create accepts an active leased snapshot as initial state, creating a slot nobody can acquire or drop

BACKUP-7.title: Base backup Send_Position declares the tli column as int4 where PostgreSQL 14 through 18 declare int8

CLIENT-1.title: Scoped Receive_Extended_Event puts an open pipelined batch into Recovery_Required on an earlier batch's error

CLIENT-2.title: Extended COPY IN counts the Sync the backend discards, leaving the session one ReadyForQuery short

CLIENT-3.title: Scoped Send_Query writes a simple query while pipeline mode is active

CLIENT-4.title: A RowDescription for another statement makes the executed portal's DataRows unreadable

CLIENT-5.title: One session-wide suspended-portal flag rejects executing and resuming portals in the same batch

CLIENT-6.title: A rejected plaintext startup leaves the session in Not_Started and accepts a second startup packet

EXAMPLES-1.title: pgish answers LIKE '%' with an internal XX000 error carrying a GNAT runtime source location

EXAMPLES-10.title: pgish answers a semicolon, comment or whitespace-only query with 42601 instead of EmptyQueryResponse

EXAMPLES-11.title: pgish returns a zero-column row for SELECT * with no FROM clause instead of rejecting it

EXAMPLES-2.title: pgish evaluates NOT LIKE as LIKE and returns the inverse row set with no diagnostic

EXAMPLES-3.title: pgish ORDER BY compares integer columns as text while WHERE compares them numerically

EXAMPLES-4.title: psqlish raises Constraint_Error on a zero-column result and abandons the connection

EXAMPLES-5.title: pgish information_schema.columns exceeds the 32-row bound unless a table_name equality filter is supplied

EXAMPLES-6.title: pgish case-folds double-quoted identifiers and accepts any table or schema qualifier

EXAMPLES-7.title: pgish keeps a session slot after an abrupt disconnect, then refuses live clients with FATAL 28P01

EXAMPLES-8.title: flyology_pgish option and environment errors escape the main handler and print a GNAT traceback

EXAMPLES-9.title: psqlish expanded output pads each field name to its column's data width instead of the widest name

LOGICAL-1.title: Logical.Producer emits a data message without the streamed xid prefix inside an open stream segment

LOGICAL-2.title: Logical.Producer ends the top-level transaction on a subtransaction Stream Abort and bars interleaving

LOGICAL-3.title: Logical.Producer rejects a non-transactional logical decoding message outside a transaction

LOGICAL-4.title: Logical.Producer accepts a Commit whose commit LSN disagrees with the pending Begin's final LSN

LOGICAL-5.title: Abort_LSN and Event_Timestamp raise on a Stream Abort built with version-4 metadata by Make_Stream_Abort

PROTO-1.title: Framing.Read_Message promises a single deadline but re-arms the full Timeout for each of its three reads

PROTO-2.title: Startup_Data, Process_Id and Secret_Key return record defaults instead of the documented Protocol_Error

PROTO-3.title: Decode_Initial is documented as taking the complete packet but decodes the bytes after the length field

PROTO-4.title: Startup replication values are matched case-sensitively, rejecting spellings PostgreSQL accepts

PROTO-5.title: Startup _pq_. protocol options are discarded, so a server cannot answer with NegotiateProtocolVersion

PROTO-6.title: Read_C_String reports a size-limit violation for an empty buffer instead of a missing terminator

PROTO-7.title: Maximum_Message_Size is documented as a frame bound but typed messages may be one byte larger

REPL-1.title: Decode_Command rejects the valueless TWO_PHASE and FAILOVER options PostgreSQL subscribers send

REPL-2.title: Decode_Command rejects the TEMPORARY and PHYSICAL forms of CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT that pg_basebackup sends

REPL-3.title: Read_Standby_Message raises Protocol_Error on the standby-initiated CopyDone PostgreSQL treats as normal

REPL-4.title: Replication SHOW rejects the dotted GUC names PostgreSQL's replication grammar accepts

REPL-5.title: Send_Identify_System advertises the IDENTIFY_SYSTEM timeline column as int4 for PostgreSQL 16 and newer peers

SCRAM-1.title: SCRAM server answers every role without a verifier using one fixed salt published in the library source

SCRAM-2.title: Optional SCRAM extension attributes are rejected in client-first, client-final and server-final messages

SCRAM-3.title: Parsing refuses SCRAM iteration counts below 4096, locking out PostgreSQL roles with a lower scram_iterations

SERVER-1.title: Run_Session's first Read_Initial runs in the declarative part, so a bare TCP probe terminates the server

SERVER-11.title: Request_Shutdown cancels no connection work with the default Drain_Timeout, so Serve never returns

SERVER-2.title: TLS_Required rejects a plaintext CancelRequest, so psql's Ctrl-C never cancels a running query

SERVER-3.title: NegotiateProtocolVersion carries the bare minor number instead of the full protocol version word

SERVER-4.title: Read_Copy_Command rejects a Sync during COPY IN and documents results its type cannot represent

SERVER-6.title: Serve_TLS raises Program_Error where its specification documents Constraint_Error, and Serve is one-shot

SERVER-7.title: Run_Session sends raw GNAT exception text to peers, and a shutdown-cancelled session gets no diagnostic

SERVER-8.title: Read_Initial has no startup-specific length bound, so four unauthenticated bytes commit a 16 MiB buffer

SERVER-9.title: TLS_Socket_Transport.Receive_Exactly changes its exception and zero-timeout behaviour given an observer

SQL-1.title: E'\v' unescapes to the letter v instead of vertical tab on PostgreSQL 17 and 18

SQL-2.title: Octal escapes E'\400' through E'\777' fail the parse with a GNAT range-check message

SQL-3.title: \U escapes at or above 0x80000000 overflow Natural and report a GNAT overflow message

SQL-4.title: Escape strings whose octal or hex escapes form invalid UTF-8 are accepted instead of rejected

SQL-5.title: UESCAPE accepts form feed on every major and vertical tab on PostgreSQL 17 and 18

SQL-6.title: On PostgreSQL 14, SELECT -'abc' folds the sign into the constant instead of building an A_Expr

SQL-7.title: Grammar-level ereport diagnostics keep the raw %s format and report the wrong cursor

SQL-8.title: Scanner diagnostics quote the rest of the statement instead of the offending token

SQL-8b.title: PostgreSQL 18's parameter-number range check is applied to PostgreSQL 14 through 17

SQL-9.title: Diagnostic cursor positions are byte offsets where PostgreSQL reports character offsets
